decisionPanels.title: 🧠 Guardian AI Strategy PIVOT — From Products to Training (Moran RISJ Quote, March 30)
decisionPanels.summary: NEW TONIGHT. The Reuters Institute published (this week) the full summary of Chris Moran's session at the RISJ AI and Future of News 2026 conference (March 17). The key quote had not previously been captured in full: 'About a year ago I realised the really consequential AI tools weren't the experimental ones we were building, but the generic systems any journalist could open in a browser.' Moran explicitly stated that Guardian *shifted focus from building AI products to providing mandatory AI training* for all journalists — teaching them how probabilistic models work, how they rely on low-quality sources, and why reporters should be sceptical of any output. This is a more significant strategy pivot than previous RISJ summaries indicated. It means: (a) The Guardian is NOT currently building new reader-facing AI products. (b) The internal tools (archive search, transcription, document analysis — per the March 4 GenAI policy page) are the approved path. (c) The political stance tracker may still be live or in pilot, but Moran's frame is now 'training journalists to use AI safely' not 'building AI features for readers.' MMR IMPLICATION: this strengthens the internal-tools positioning. MMR is the data infrastructure that INTERNAL tools (archive chatbot, transcription) depend on. Position it that way to leadership — not as 'AI product data layer' but as 'the foundation for safe, accountable internal AI use of Guardian content.'
actions: REFRAME MMR pitch to leadership: not 'AI product data layer' but 'the foundation for Guardian's internal AI tools (archive search, transcription, document analysis).' Moran's framing is now the institutional language.
READ: theguardian.com/help/insideguardian/2026/mar/04/how-the-guardian-is-using-genai — the approved in-house tools list. Identify which ones need iconik metadata. Archive search is confirmed.
ASK editorial innovation: does the internal archive search tool index multimedia/video from iconik? (Still the key unresolved question.)

USE in leadership: 'Guardian's AI strategy is now training journalists to use generic tools responsibly + building safe internal tools. MMR ensures that when internal tools query the archive, the multimedia metadata is complete, structured, and AI-retrievable.'

decisionPanels.title: 🎥 GoPro GP3 Cameras at NAB April 19 — Biggest Upgrade in Years
decisionPanels.summary: NEW TONIGHT. GoPro announced (March 25) it will unveil multiple new cameras at NAB 2026 (April 19-22, Booth C5519) powered by the next-generation GP3 processor — described by CEO Nicholas Woodman as 'the most significant leap in GoPro's imaging technology to date.' The GP3 processor doubles pixel processing capacity and enables entirely new camera categories beyond GoPro's traditional action-camera lane. T3 notes the NAB announcement 'confirms GoPro will showcase several new cameras, not just one' — this is a platform expansion, not an incremental product refresh. Strategic relevance for Guardian: field journalists and Guardian Studios use action cameras for social-native content. If GP3 opens a new category (likely: higher-quality social-first content camera, possibly vertical-native), this is relevant for MMR workflows and Project Launcher output types. Guardian field teams should be briefed after NAB.
actions: WATCH NAB: GoPro Booth C5519 (April 19-22). Multiple new cameras — understand the new categories, not just the spec sheet.
POST-NAB: if GP3 opens a 'social-first' camera category, add to Project Launcher roadmap as a supported ingest format.
CONTEXT: GoPro's NAB move suggests a deliberate upmarket push — this could overlap with Guardian's documentary/field journalism use case, not just extreme sports.

decisionPanels.title: ☁️ Suite Studios S3 GA in April — Validate LucidLink Strategy
decisionPanels.summary: Suite Studios S3 Native File Streaming goes GA in April 2026 (per Blocks & Files Feb 17). LucidLink advantages: full Filespace ecosystem (Connect + Guest Access + Directory API), Emmy award, established customer base. Suite advantage: zero proprietary client required.

LucidLink Connect is the recommended choice: depth of ecosystem, proven scale. But flag the competition exists.
